00-README.title: OPS GTM bundle, Austin Ten Operator Program
00-README.html:
OPS GTM bundle, Austin Ten Operator Program

Everything Kevin needs to run the One Person Show go to market sprint. OPS is the office layer for solo and small crew service operators: consumables, field, and vehicle businesses that run on a recurring cadence. Site: ops.greenguard-usa.com.

Who owns what

  • Kevin owns: target research review, outreach sends from his own mailbox, discovery calls, weekly check ins with the ten operators, baseline metrics capture, the objection and competitive logs, the weekly report to Dan.
  • Claude drafts: every outreach email and sequence step, the discovery script, positioning review worksheets, the KPI rollups, the case study draft. Claude never sends.
  • Dan approves and sends: every outreach email before it goes out, every target row before the first touch, pricing exceptions, the published case study, anything that commits the company to an operator.
  • Dan does on site: the Mac mini or managed appliance setup at each of the ten operators, the real install.sh run, and any hands on network or Workspace configuration the operator cannot do themselves.

Read in this order

  1. 01-plan/ops-90-day-gtm-sprint.md, the playbook.
  2. 04-program/ten-operator-program.md, the offer being extended.
  3. 05-icp-INTERNAL.md, who qualifies.
  4. 06-targets/operator-targets.csv, the researched list, blank until Dan approves rows.
  5. 07-outreach/, first email and sequence.
  6. 08-discovery-and-baseline.md, the call script and the metrics form.
  7. 09-objection-library.md, 10-competitive-cheat-sheet.md.
  8. 11-reports/, weekly report and KPI template.
  9. 12-positioning/, the reviewed copy and worksheets.
  10. 13-implementation-playbook-INTERNAL.md, filled in as each setup happens.
  11. 15-product-calendar.md, what Kevin can promise.

Three rules that override everything else

  1. Dan approves every target row before the first touch, and sends every email himself.
  2. Copy stays trade neutral: consumables, field, vehicle, never a specific trade name inside this bundle's outward facing copy.
  3. Pricing facts come from this bundle and ops.greenguard-usa.com only: Starter $99, Office $249, Crew $449, managed Mac $59 a month or $1,200 once, setup $500 or $1,500.

01-plan/ops-90-day-gtm-sprint.title: OPS 90-Day Go-to-Market Sprint
01-plan/ops-90-day-gtm-sprint.html:
OPS 90-Day Go-to-Market Sprint

Ten Operator Program, Austin metro, 2026-09-07

Objective: place OPS with ten real Austin metro owner operators, capture baseline office hours and revenue metrics before and after, and produce the first case study that proves the office hours reduction claim.

Primary owner: Kevin. Duration: 90 days.

1. Mission

The job is not to sell ten monthly subscriptions in 90 days. The job is to run a disciplined validation sprint that answers:

  1. Which owner operators have the office burden OPS removes?
  2. Which setup steps take real hours, and how many?
  3. What breaks in a live operator's stack that a demo never shows?
  4. What is the true cost basis for a setup fee?
  5. Does office hours per week actually drop, and by how much?
  6. Can one case study, with real numbers, carry the next fifty targets?

2. Core principle

Do not sell software. Sell the hours back:

What would you do with ten hours a week back?

Messaging: the trade stays yours, the office becomes ours. Nothing gets replaced on day one. Keep Google Workspace and Stripe. Replace the manual work between them.

3. What success looks like at day 90

Minimum: 3 tenants live 30 or more days, baseline metrics captured on all 10 applicants, objection log started. Target: 5 tenants live, 1 case study published, measurable office hours reduction on 3 operators. Exceptional: 8 tenants live, 2 case studies, a repeatable onboarding playbook other operators can self serve.

4. Approved targets

06-targets/operator-targets.csv carries 30 to 50 Austin metro owner operator candidates researched from public sources. Dan approves each row before the first touch.

5. Week one: immersion

Days 1 to 3: product and pricing

Read 04-program/ten-operator-program.md, 05-icp-INTERNAL.md, and the OPS product definition. Know the three tiers cold: Starter $99, Office $249, Crew $449, managed Mac $59 a month or $1,200 once, setup $500 or $1,500.

Days 4 to 7: positioning review

Read all of 12-positioning/. Be able to explain the private office computer architecture in one sentence: the owner's Mac runs the back office on a flat subscription, nothing routes through a shared cloud seat.

6. Honest limits

  • No published case study yet until day 60. Say so.
  • The Ten Operator Program is invitation only and time limited; it is not the standard price.
  • Setup is done in person or remote by Dan; Kevin schedules it.
  • HVAC is out of scope for this sprint; recurring cadence trades only.

7. Days 1 to 14: narrow ICP and build the front door

Finalize the ICP in 05-icp-INTERNAL.md. Ship the homepage "Who this is for" copy and the Before vs After copy (12-positioning/homepage-who-this-is-for.md, 12-positioning/before-vs-after.md). Build the baseline metrics form (08-discovery-and-baseline.md). Draft the payroll and bookkeeping positioning review worksheets (12-positioning/payroll-positioning-review.md, 12-positioning/bookkeeping-positioning-review.md) and get them reviewed before any operator sees them. Research and get Dan's approval on 30 to 50 targets. Send the first touches. Write the proof endpoint spec, a simple page or API response an operator's own site can point to that shows OPS is live and working for them.

8. Score every target

Criteria Score
Recurring cadence fit 0 to 5
Google Workspace and Stripe fit 0 to 5
Size band fit 0 to 5
Office pain evidence 0 to 5
Owner operated 0 to 5
Review volume 0 to 5
Reachability 0 to 5

Maximum 35. Tier A 25 to 35, direct outreach. Tier B 18 to 24, secondary. Tier C under 18, monitor.

9. Days 1 to 14: first touches and proof endpoint

The 06-targets/operator-targets.csv list is scored and approved. Outreach begins once Dan approves rows. See 07-outreach/first-email.md and 07-outreach/sequence.md. In parallel, ship the proof endpoint: a live, working piece of the product an applicant can see before they commit.

10. Days 1 to 14: baseline metrics and reviews

Every applicant that responds completes the baseline metrics form before onboarding: office hours per week, quote turnaround, close rate, days to paid, reminder coverage, missed visits per month, revenue, active accounts. The payroll and bookkeeping positioning reviews are finished and approved by day 14, not after.

11. Days 15 to 90: applications and acceptance

Target 10 completed applications, 5 accepted into the Ten Operator Program. Acceptance criteria in 04-program/ten-operator-program.md.

12. Days 15 to 90: implementations

3 to 5 deep implementations. Each logged in 13-implementation-playbook-INTERNAL.md: hours spent, what failed, which tasks were Dan's and which were Claude's. This log is the pricing cost basis for setup fees going forward.

13. Days 15 to 90: feature usage log

Track which OPS features each live tenant actually touches weekly. Feeds the KPI rollup and tells Kevin which tiers are underused.

14. Days 15 to 90: onboarding playbook

Turn the first 3 implementations into a repeatable playbook and an intake form so the fourth and fifth onboarding take less time than the first.

15. Days 1 to 14: proof endpoint spec

Written spec for a small, real, verifiable piece of the product, for example a live customer portal page or a status endpoint, that a prospective operator or Dan can point to as evidence OPS runs in production today.

16. Days 15 to 90: implementation cost capture

Every implementation records actual hours against the $500 and $1,500 setup fee tiers. If actual hours consistently exceed the fee, flag it to Dan before the next signup.

17. Days 15 to 90: first case study

Target operator day 60: one tenant with 30 plus days live, clean before and after baseline numbers, and permission to publish. Draft in 13-implementation-playbook-INTERNAL.md format, reviewed by Dan before anything goes out.

18. Days 15 to 90: pricing refined from real hours

Once 3 or more implementations are logged, revisit the $500 or $1,500 setup fee split against real hours from section 16, and recommend an adjustment to Dan if the numbers say so.

19. Days 15 to 90: private office computer messaging

Finalize 12-positioning/private-office-computer.md using real operator reactions from discovery calls. This message differentiates OPS from every SaaS competitor: the operator's own Mac, not a shared cloud seat, runs their back office.

20. Weekly operating rhythm

Monday: pipeline review, applications, baseline captures, implementation status. Tuesday to Thursday: outreach, discovery calls, onboarding, implementation work. Friday: one page weekly report to Dan (11-reports/weekly-report-template.md).

21. Objection and competitive logs

Build 09-objection-library.md and 10-competitive-cheat-sheet.md from every conversation. Review weekly with Dan.

22. KPI dashboard

Applications, accepted, baselines captured, tenants live, case study published. Template in 11-reports/kpi-template.md.

23. What Kevin should not do

Do not discount below the Ten Operator Program terms. Do not promise a feature not on the product calendar. Do not send an email Dan has not approved. Do not call OPS a CRM or a payroll provider.

24. Product calendar

See 15-product-calendar.md for what Kevin can promise during the sprint.

25. Access checklist before day 1

Google Workspace mailbox and calendar access, the approved target sheet, this bundle, a standing weekly slot with Dan.

26. Required deliverables at day 90

Market validation report, ICP refinement, objection report, competitive intelligence, tenant pipeline status, product feedback themes, recommended next phase strategy.

27. Timeline

Days Phase Output
Days 1 to 3 Learn the product: pricing, tiers, positioning Kevin can explain OPS unprompted
Days 3 to 7 Narrow ICP written ICP finalized in 05-icp-INTERNAL.md
Days 5 to 10 Who-this-is-for and before vs after copy drafted Homepage copy ready for review
Days 7 to 14 Payroll and bookkeeping positioning reviews Worksheets and disclaimers approved
Days 7 to 14 Baseline metrics form live Form ready to capture day 0 numbers
Days 10 to 14 Targets researched and Dan approved Approved rows in 06-targets/operator-targets.csv
Days 12 to 14 First touches sent Outreach live on approved rows
Days 14 to 14 Proof endpoint spec written Spec ready to build against
Days 15 to 30 Applications and acceptances 10 applications, 5 accepted
Days 20 to 45 First deep implementations 3 to 5 tenants onboarded
Days 30 to 60 Playbook and intake built Repeatable onboarding playbook and intake form
Days 45 to 75 Feature usage log and cost capture Usage tracked, setup hours logged against fee
Days 60 to 75 First case study drafted Draft with day 0 to day 60 numbers, pending Dan approval
Days 75 to 90 Pricing refined and architecture messaging shipped Pricing checked against real hours, private office computer messaging finalized
Days 91 to 120 Scale, gated on 3 tenants live 30 plus days, 1 case study, measurable office hours reduction on 3 operators: marketing scale up, vertical landing pages, referral program, implementation partner program, price move to list, widen ICP, job based verticals Scale plan approved by Dan

Final instruction

Your job is not to prove OPS is amazing. Your job is to discover where it is genuinely valuable, capture the real numbers, and hand Dan a case study he can point to.

04-program/ten-operator-program.title: Ten Operator Program
04-program/ten-operator-program.html:
Ten Operator Program

Ten Austin metro owner operators. Office tier free for 90 days, then $149 a month locked for year one. Setup fee waived.

In exchange

  • A weekly 20 minute check in with Kevin.
  • Baseline metrics captured at day 0, 30, 60, and 90.
  • Permission to use anonymized results in a case study.

Acceptance criteria

Recurring cadence service business in the Austin metro area, solo or 1 to 3 crew, already using Google Workspace and Stripe, at least 40 recurring accounts. Application reviewed by Kevin, accepted rows approved by Dan.

What happens after 90 days

At day 90 the operator moves to the standard Office tier, $249 a month, unless Dan approves an extension. The $149 lock is for year one only from acceptance date, not from signup.

05-icp-INTERNAL.title: ICP, internal
05-icp-INTERNAL.html:
ICP, internal

Solo or 1 to 3 crew. Recurring cadence service business (weekly, biweekly, or monthly visits), not one off jobs. Revenue $80,000 to $300,000 a year. Already on Google Workspace and Stripe. At least 40 recurring accounts. Austin metro first.

HVAC is out for now: seasonal and one off call volume does not match the recurring cadence assumption OPS is built around.

07-outreach/first-email.title: First outreach email
07-outreach/first-email.html:
First outreach email

Audience: the owner of one of the target operators (see 06-targets/operator-targets.csv). Voice: company voice, terse, no hype, no em dashes. One ask. Sent from Kevin's mailbox only after Dan approves the row.

Subject

Ten hours a week back, for ten Austin operators

Body

Hello {first name},

GreenGuard USA built the office side of a recurring service business into a product: quoting, booking, reminders, invoicing, the books, and payroll, running on a flat monthly cost instead of a stack of SaaS seats.

We are inviting ten Austin metro owner operators into a Ten Operator Program: the Office tier free for 90 days, then locked at $149 a month for year one, setup fee waived, in exchange for a 20 minute weekly check in and permission to use your before and after numbers, anonymized, in a case study.

Would a short call make sense in the next two weeks?

{Kevin's signature} GreenGuard USA

Follow-up, seven days later, if no reply

Subject: Re: Ten hours a week back, for ten Austin operators

Hello {first name}, one line in case the first note was buried. If the office side of your business is not the bottleneck right now, a one word reply saves us both a second follow-up.

Goal of the conversation

A completed baseline metrics form and, if there is fit, an application to the Ten Operator Program.

07-outreach/sequence.title: Outreach sequence (four touches)
07-outreach/sequence.html:
Outreach sequence (four touches)

Rules: one named person per firm at a time, Dan has approved the row, plain text, no attachments on touch 1 or 2, log every send. Company voice, no hype, no em dashes.

Touch 1, day 0: the hours question

Subject: Ten hours a week back, for ten Austin operators

Hello {first name}, {one sentence tied to something public about their business}. We built the office side of a recurring service business into one product and are inviting ten Austin metro owner operators to try it, free for 90 days. Would a short call make sense in the next two weeks?

Touch 2, day 3 to 5: the specific observation

Subject: Re: Ten hours a week back, for ten Austin operators

Hello {first name}, one specific thing: {an observation from their site or reviews showing recurring cadence, for example route density or review volume}. That is exactly the kind of schedule where the office work eats the most hours. Is there a good time this week?

Touch 3, day 8 to 10: one asset

Pick exactly one: the homepage "Who this is for" page, or the Before vs After page.

Subject: Re: Ten hours a week back, for ten Austin operators

Hello {first name}, no pitch, one page: {link}. If it is not relevant right now, a one word reply saves us both a further note.

Touch 4, only after relevance is established: the program

Subject: OPS Ten Operator Program

Hello {first name}, thanks for the conversation. We have a few seats left in the Ten Operator Program, free for 90 days, setup fee waived. Would you like to apply?

Handling replies

Any reply: log it, respond within one business day. "Not relevant": close, cancel remaining touches. "Send me more": send exactly one asset. Silence after touch 4: 60 day hold.

08-discovery-and-baseline.title: Discovery script and baseline metrics form
08-discovery-and-baseline.html:
Discovery script and baseline metrics form

Discovery script

Owner speaks most of the call. Open with: "This is a discovery call, not a demo. I want to understand how the office side of your business runs today."

Questions:

  1. How many hours a week go to the office side: quoting, scheduling, invoicing, follow up, books?
  2. How long does a quote take from request to sent, and from sent to accepted?
  3. What share of quotes close?
  4. How many days from invoice to paid, on average?
  5. How do you remind customers of upcoming visits today?
  6. How many missed visits a month, and why?
  7. What is annual revenue and how many active recurring accounts do you have?

Baseline metrics form

Captured at day 0, 30, 60, and 90 for every applicant and every live tenant.

Metric Day 0 Day 30 Day 60 Day 90
Office hours per week
Quote turnaround (request to sent)
Close rate
Days to paid
Reminder coverage (percent of visits reminded)
Missed visits per month
Revenue

09-objection-library.title: Objection library
09-objection-library.html:
Objection library

Categories: Product, Commercial, Market, Trust. Add every new objection in the operator's exact words. Review weekly with Dan.

# Category Objection (exact words) Frequency Severity Response Product action
1 Commercial "What happens after the free 90 days?" Locked at $149 a month for year one, then standard Office tier pricing unless Dan approves an extension. none
2 Trust "Is my data safe on your Mac?" The office computer is dedicated to the operator's own business, not a shared cloud account. See the private office computer positioning page. none
3 Market "I already use a scheduling app." OPS replaces the manual work between the apps, not necessarily the calendar itself; discovery call determines the real overlap. none
4 Trust "Are you a payroll provider?" No. OPS prepares payroll worksheets your provider files. See the payroll positioning review. none
5 Trust "Are you my accountant?" No. OPS prepares a close your CPA reviews. See the bookkeeping positioning review. none

12-positioning/before-vs-after.title: Before vs After
12-positioning/before-vs-after.html:
Before vs After

Before

Quotes typed by hand, sent late. Invoices chased. Reminders sent when remembered. The books done on a weekend, months behind. Payroll worksheets built from memory. Evenings spent on the office instead of the trade or family.

After

Quotes sent same day, self-serve pay and book link included. Invoices generated per visit. Reminders sent automatically. The books categorized and closed monthly, ready for your CPA. Payroll worksheets ready for your provider. Evenings back.

12-positioning/bookkeeping-positioning-r.title: Bookkeeping positioning review
12-positioning/bookkeeping-positioning-r.html:
Bookkeeping positioning review

Required disclaimer on every bookkeeping facing page and conversation: we are not a CPA firm.

OPS imports bank transactions, categorizes them, and prepares a monthly close. Your CPA reviews and files. OPS does not provide tax advice and does not replace your CPA.

Close prepared for your CPA

  • Categorized transaction ledger for the month.
  • Monthly profit and loss summary.
  • Outstanding invoices and expenses flagged for review.

Review status: draft, needs Dan approval before use in any operator facing conversation.

12-positioning/homepage-who-this-is-for.title: Homepage: Who this is for
12-positioning/homepage-who-this-is-for.html:
Homepage: Who this is for

You run a recurring service business: consumables, field crews, or a vehicle on the road every week. You already do the trade well. The office is the part that eats your evenings: quoting, scheduling, reminders, invoicing, the books, payroll.

OPS is the office. One private computer, one flat monthly cost, running your back office 24/7 so you can stay on the trade.

This is built for owner operators with 0 to 3 crew doing $80,000 to $300,000 a year, already using Google Workspace and Stripe, with 40 or more recurring accounts.

12-positioning/payroll-positioning-revie.title: Payroll positioning review
12-positioning/payroll-positioning-revie.html:
Payroll positioning review

Required disclaimer on every payroll facing page and conversation: we are not a payroll provider.

OPS prepares timesheets, overtime calculations, and 941, 940, and W-2 worksheets. Your payroll provider files them. OPS does not remit taxes, does not file on your behalf, and does not replace your provider.

Worksheet the operator's provider files

  • Employee hours by pay period, regular and overtime.
  • Gross pay by employee.
  • Quarterly 941 worksheet.
  • Annual 940 worksheet.
  • Year end W-2 worksheet.

Review status: draft, needs Dan approval before use in any operator facing conversation.

12-positioning/private-office-computer.title: Private office computer
12-positioning/private-office-computer.html:
Private office computer

OPS runs on a computer dedicated to the operator's own business, not a shared cloud seat. The owner's data, customer records, and back office logic stay on that machine, connected only to the operator's own Google Workspace and Stripe accounts.

This is the architecture message: one private office computer per operator, running on a flat monthly cost, versus a stack of shared SaaS seats billed per feature and per employee.

13-implementation-playbook-INTERNAL.html:

  • What failed during setup, and how it was resolved.

  • Notes for the next tenant's onboarding, folded into the repeatable playbook and intake form.
